text: A PSS can work if it operates at 2.4 Gigs using one of these frequency channels. Now this means that the base station, sorry, the access point, and all the users connected to that access point will operate using the same frequency channel. Okay, it can be this one, or this one, or this one, if we work at 2.4 Gigs. So scanning, that is our first step, allows users to discover an access point that is available nearby. How can this happen? Let's assume that we enter the campus. Then our Wi-Fi card will start listening, if it operates at 2.4 Gigs, to this first frequency channel. And if there are access points operating on these frequency channels, our Wi-Fi card will be able to discover them. How? Because every access point periodically broadcasts a packet called beacon.
